title: Knowing Louis Armstrong and the Fletcher Henderson band in New York
summary: DeDroit says Armstrong was his friend, dedicated a number to him in New Orleans, and was held back in Fletcher Henderson's arranged band in New York.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: But did you know Louis Armstrong? Did you ever know him?

I knew him personally. He was my friend. Well when he was at the play down here, I was listening to him and he says, I'd like to dedicate this next number to my little fat friend, Johnny Gidroyd. I was a little star at that time, you know, and he called me his fat. And then I met him in New York, and we were palsy-weldy, and I loved to hear him play. And when he was on the coast, my brother used to go out to the cotton club and they were friends. And he was one of the finest men I ever met, I mean as far as I know.
But did you know him in New York you say?

Yes, he was playing with Fletcher Henderson, a band that played strictly arrangements. Lewis was lost in that band. That's why I said, Fletcher, won't you let Lewis do, it don't mean a thing if you ain't got that swing and Lewis, you know. And Lewis did it. The place woke up, they came alive.
What year was that? Do you remember?
